review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the Mathlib tree for uses of the candidate lemmas. The only uses are inside this file. I found no simp attributes in the file, so no rewrite loops, competing rules or bad orientations are possible. The findings are therefore about missing simp lemmas. I did not run Lean, so the simp-normal-form claims come from reading the statements. Both findings are low-to-moderate confidence because there are no downstream uses that currently need the simp lemmas.

findings.excerpt:
lemma depth_eq_top_of_subsingleton (N M : ModuleCat.{v} R) [Subsingleton M] :
    N.depth M = ⊤ := by
findings.problem: These three lemmas have the same shape. The left side is a `depth` application whose only hypothesis is the instance `[Subsingleton M]`. The right side is the constant `⊤`, so the lemmas are terminating, they have a canonical normal form, and `simp` can discharge the hypothesis by instance synthesis. None of them is tagged `@[simp]`. A goal such as `N.depth (ModuleCat.of R PUnit) = ⊤` or `I.depth 0 = ⊤` therefore needs a manual `rw`/`exact` with the right namespace variant. The three variants also have no marked relation to each other.
findings.proposed_change: Mark all three as `@[simp]`. The `ModuleCat`, `Ideal` and `IsLocalRing` variants have disjoint head symbols, so they do not compete. Alternatively, mark only the general `ModuleCat.depth_eq_top_of_subsingleton` and state the `Ideal`/`IsLocalRing` versions through `Ideal.depth`/`IsLocalRing.depth` unfolding. The first option is simpler.
findings.benefit: Depth statements about zero or trivial modules, such as `Ideal.depth` of a zero module or of the cokernel of a surjection, would normalise to `⊤` under `simp`. Users would not need to remember three differently namespaced lemma names.

findings.excerpt:
((ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{w} R).obj N).depth ((ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{w} R).obj M) =
    N.depth M
findings.problem: Both lemmas are universe-change identities whose right side is strictly simpler than the left. `depth_uliftFunctor_obj` removes the `uliftFunctor` from both arguments, and `Ideal.depth_shrink` (line 420) replaces `Shrink R` by `R`. Neither is a simp lemma. The proof of `depth_eq_of_linearEquiv` has to apply `depth_uliftFunctor_obj` by hand, with `rw [← ...]` and explicit arguments. Any other goal that mentions `depth` after a `uliftFunctor` or `Shrink` therefore needs the same manual rewriting.
findings.proposed_change: Consider tagging `ModuleCat.depth_uliftFunctor_obj` and `Ideal.depth_shrink` with `@[simp]`. Both reduce the term size and neither side can rewrite back. For `depth_uliftFunctor_obj`, check that the `Small.{max v w} R` instance argument is found by instance synthesis, since it is not determined by the left side. If it is not found, leave the lemma non-simp.
findings.benefit: Depth computations that pass through `ULift`/`Shrink` would normalise to the base module automatically. The proof of `depth_eq_of_linearEquiv` would also have a simp-friendly entry point.
